synthesis:draft.headline: MAE 32.88 MW (ev1538); mean error 4.88 MW (ev1539); largest absolute error 66.0 MW at 2026-07-30 15:30 UTC (ev1476)
summary: MAE over the 24 half-hours (2026-07-30 11:00 UTC to 2026-07-30 23:00 UTC) was 32.88 MW [ev1538].
Mean error over that window was 4.88 MW (POE50 minus actual) [ev1539].
The largest absolute half-hour forecast error was 66.0 MW at 2026-07-30 15:30 UTC (ev1476) [ev1476].
Two consecutive half-hours exceeded the South Australia review threshold of 50 MW: 66.0 MW at 2026-07-30 15:30 UTC (ev1476) and 51.0 MW at 2026-07-30 16:00 UTC (ev1480) (see procedure citation c1).
System context at the 5-minute price peak (2026-07-31 02:05 ACST): RRP $4981.0/MWh [ev0989] and TOTALDEMAND 1472.82 MW [ev0990].
The half-hour containing the price extreme (peak_half_hour_end_utc 2026-07-30T17:00:00Z = 2026-07-31 02:30 ACST) had operational demand 1466.0 MW [ev0532].
The window maximum operational demand (within 2026-07-30T04:30:00Z to 2026-07-31T05:00:00Z) was 2173.0 MW at 2026-07-30 09:30 UTC [ev0517].
During the same window there were 214 five-minute intervals at-or-above the analysis threshold of $300.0/MWh [ev1440][ev1441].

possible_explanations.statement: Forecast error magnitude may be related to weather-forecast differences; see the procedure note that demand forecast accuracy is dependent on weather forecast accuracy [c2].
possible_explanations.what_would_test_it: Compare the weather forecasts used by the DFS for 2026-07-30 with observed weather for SA1 during the same intervals and check whether forecast deviations correlate with forecast errors.

possible_explanations.statement: Forecast error may be associated with net interchange or unusual interconnector flows (the net interchange at the 5-minute peak was -82.59 MW) and could explain part of demand deviations.
possible_explanations.what_would_test_it: Examine half-hourly net interchange and regional demand pairs across the errorful intervals to see if unforecasted interchange changes coincide with the POE50 minus actual errors.

possible_explanations.statement: Large price spikes and many intervals above the analysis threshold might be coincident with demand deviations and could indicate tight supply conditions; review pricing and generator availability (see price evidence ev0989 and intervals-at-threshold ev1440).
possible_explanations.what_would_test_it: Compare generator availability, constraint reports and rebid/market notices for the intervals with high prices and large demand forecast errors to see whether supply-side changes temporally align with the forecast errors.
